subject: Private deployment exhibits + order form language for snapshot / operator access
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@luminahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@luminahealth.com>, Lumina Health Procurement <procurement@luminahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy — exhibits, operator access window, and order form ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and procurement reviewed the MSA + Order Form and have a few outstanding items for any on-prem/VPC addendum:

- We need a short exhibit describing the mechanism for transfers of environment snapshots and the attestation that Redwood retained no customer data post-transfer.
- Clarify operator access windows and a process for temporary audit console access (including advance notice and scoped credentials).
- We would like an "escrow-lite" option: a sealed artifact + independent custodian attestation if Redwood is winding down or the contract terminates.

Attached is a redlined draft our GC started (high level) and a sample procurement timeline. Can Redwood confirm whether the snapshot handback can be performed as a one-time S3 transfer + signed manifest, and if you support HSM-wrapped keys for secrets handed to our custodian?

Tom (cc) will be our main legal contact for redlines. Looking to get this agreed before final signature the week of Mar 8.

Appreciate any detail you can share so procurement can clear internal approvals.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Procurement, Lumina Health
Attachment: lumina-deploy-exhibits-proposed-redlines.pdf (PDF, 112 KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 13:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy — exhibits, operator access window, and order form ask

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list and for the draft.

High level answers up front:
- Snapshot handback: yes, we can provide a one-time object transfer (S3/GS) with a signed manifest and checksum. We propose including a transfer acceptance checklist in the Order Form as an Exhibit.
- HSM-wrapped keys: we support exporting encrypted key material wrapped to a customer key or custodian key using standard wrapping (PKCS#11). We will need the custodian's public key and an acceptance test plan in the SOW.
- Operator access windows & audit access: Redwood can offer time-limited bastion sessions and scoped console tokens with advance notice (48 hours suggested). For audits, we can provide a temporary monitoring-only role and a scrubbed console snapshot for offline review.

Karthik — can you propose defensible language for the Order Form Exhibit and a short attestation clause for the "escrow-lite" scenario? Lauren, can you confirm whether we should route any of this through our security operations team for a write-up they can share with Lumina legal?

We can target a redline package by Fri, Mar 5 to give them a few days before Mar 8 approvals.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: runbook-sample-ops.txt (text, 6 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@luminahealth.com>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@luminahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy — exhibits, operator access window, and order form ask

Tessa / team — drafting notes below; flagged items that will likely require Lumina signoff.

1) Order Form Exhibit language (proposed short form):
- "Snapshot Transfer Exhibit: Upon termination or expiry and where Customer elects, Redwood will provide a one-time transfer of Customer environment data ("Snapshot") to a mutually agreed object store. Transfer will be accompanied by a signed manifest and SHA256 checksums. Redwood will perform a verified deletion of Customer data from Redwood-managed systems within thirty (30) days of successful transfer and will provide Customer with an attestation of deletion signed by an authorized Redwood officer."

2) "Escrow-lite" attestation (proposed):
- "In circumstances where Redwood ceases to operate the Service or materially breaches the Agreement and such breach is not cured within the cure period, Redwood will deposit a sealed artifact containing operational artifacts necessary to instantiate Customer environment (configuration, model weights, runbook) with an independent custodian. The custodian shall provide an attestation of custody and will release the artifact to Customer upon demonstration of the triggering event. Redwood will provide sufficient documentation to enable a third-party engineer to restore the environment under the terms of the Exhibit."

Notes / items for Lumina:
- Custodian public key: we can wrap key material to a custodian key, but need the cert.
- Proof of deletion: our deletion attestation will reference retention logs; Lumina may ask for an external audit (SOC2 snapshot) to corroborate.
- Operator access: recommend adding a change-control step and a 72-hour notice window for higher-privilege sessions rather than 48 — reduces operational risk.

Lauren — can sec-ops produce a one-page checklist of audit artifacts and an ops contact for the attestation? We should offer either a signed attestation + console logs package or an external auditor report (SOC2 snapshot) depending on procurement appetite.

I'll assemble these redlines into a tracked-change Order Form Exhibit and send by Fri.

— Karthik
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@luminahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Patel <sara@luminahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy — exhibits, operator access window, and order form ask

Karthik / Tessa — thank you for the thoughtful language. A few comments from our side:

- The Snapshot Transfer Exhibit language looks acceptable; we will ask for the attestation to include the officer's printed name and title.
- For the escrow-lite clause, Lumina prefers the custodian to be a mutually agreed third party and to include a simple release checklist (triggering events: insolvency, persistent material breach after cure).
- Regarding the notice window for operator access, Lumina can accept 72 hours for privileged sessions. For urgent remediation we would like a documented emergency access procedure that includes: (a) phone escalation to Lumina infosec, (b) an ad-hoc temporary token with immediate expiry after session, and (c) post-session logs and signed attestation.

Please include the custodian public key field in the exhibit template and a placeholder for DocuSign signature blocks. We received internal approval to proceed on the condition we have the exhibit language finalized by Mar 9.

Tom Briggs
Senior Counsel, Lumina Health
